title.value: Tau-targeting antisense oligonucleotide MAPT Rx in mild Alzheimer’s disease: a phase 1b, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
title.quote: Tau-targeting antisense oligonucleotide MAPT Rx in mild Alzheimer’s disease: a phase 1b, randomized, placebo-controlled trial

design.value: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, multiple-ascending dose (MAD) phase 1b trial with an open-label long-term extension
design.quote: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, MAD phase 1b trial with an open-label LTE, we evaluated the safety, PK and target engagement of MAPT Rx in participants with mild AD.
design.location: Methods, Study design and participants, paragraph 1

phase.quote: We report the results of a first-in-human phase 1b clinical trial evaluating a tau-targeting ASO administered intrathecally as a bolus in adults with mild AD.

n.quote: Forty-six patients enrolled in the trial, of whom 34 were randomized to MAPT Rx and 12 to placebo.

n_description.value: randomized (46 underwent randomization out of 102 screened; 34 to MAPT Rx and 12 to placebo)
n_description.quote: From August 2017 through February 2020, 102 participants were screened for eligibility and 46 underwent randomization according to the protocol

population.value: Adults aged 50–74 years with mild AD, defined by CDR Overall Global Score of 1 or Global Score of 0.5 with a Memory Score of 1, MMSE 20–27 inclusive, a CSF pattern of low Aβ42 and elevated t-tau and p-tau, and a diagnosis of probable AD by NIA-AA criteria
population.quote: Eligible participants were between the ages of 50 and 74 years and had mild AD, defined by a CDR Overall Global Score of 1 or Global Score of 0.5 with a Memory Score of 1
population.location: Methods, Study design and participants, paragraph 2

followup.value: 13-week treatment period followed by a 23-week post-treatment period (with an optional open-label long-term extension, part 2)
followup.quote: randomized 3:1 to intrathecal bolus administrations of MAPT Rx or placebo every 4 or 12 weeks during the 13-week treatment period, followed by a 23 week post-treatment period

intervention.value: MAPT Rx (ISIS 814907/BIIB080), a tau-targeting antisense oligonucleotide, given as intrathecal bolus injections: 10 mg, 30 mg or 60 mg monthly (four doses each) or 115 mg quarterly (two doses)
intervention.quote: cohort A, 10 mg monthly, cohort B 30 mg monthly or cohort C, 60 mg monthly (total of four doses each); or cohort D, 115 mg quarterly (total of two doses)
intervention.location: Methods, Study design and participants, paragraph 3

comparator.value: placebo (artificial CSF), administered as bolus intrathecal injection, randomized 3:1 within each dose cohort; placebo group pooled for analyses
comparator.quote: A centralized automated randomization system assigned participants 3:1 to receive bolus IT injections of MAPT Rx or placebo (artificial CSF) within each of four dose cohorts
comparator.location: Methods, Study design and participants, paragraph 3

biomarker_confirmation.value: CSF pattern of low Aβ42 and elevated t-tau and p-tau consistent with a diagnosis of AD, plus diagnosis of probable AD by National Institute of Aging-Alzheimer Association criteria
biomarker_confirmation.quote: CSF pattern of low Aβ42 and elevated t-tau and p-tau consistent with diagnosis of AD; and diagnosis of probable AD based on National Institute of Aging-Alzheimer Association criteria
biomarker_confirmation.location: Methods, Study design and participants, paragraph 2

cohorts: cohort A (10 mg MAPT Rx or placebo monthly)
cohort B (30 mg MAPT Rx or placebo monthly)
cohort C (60 mg MAPT Rx or placebo monthly)
cohort D (115 mg MAPT Rx or placebo quarterly)

outcomes.name: Safety of MAPT Rx (adverse events, physical and neurologic examination, Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale, laboratory assessments, vital signs, electrocardiograms and safety MRI)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The primary endpoint was safety. The secondary endpoint was MAPT Rx pharmacokinetics in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The prespecified key exploratory outcome was CSF total-tau protein concentration.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Adverse events in 94% of MAPT Rx-treated participants versus 75% of placebo-treated participants; all mild (88%) or moderate (12%); no serious adverse events in MAPT Rx-treated participants
outcomes.quote: Adverse events were reported in 94% of MAPT Rx -treated patients and 75% of placebo-treated patients; all were mild or moderate. No serious adverse events were reported in MAPT Rx -treated patients.
outcomes.location: Abstract; Results, Primary endpoint of safety

outcomes.name: MAPT Rx pharmacokinetics in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The secondary endpoint was the characterization of the PK of MAPT Rx in CSF.
outcomes.effect_estimate: MAPT Rx measurable in CSF in all participants receiving MAPT Rx; trough concentrations increased from the 10 mg to the 30 mg and 60 mg monthly doses
outcomes.quote: MAPT Rx was measurable in the CSF in all participants receiving MAPT Rx (Fig. ). Pre-dose or trough concentrations increased from the 10 mg monthly dose to those observed at the 30 mg and 60 mg monthly doses.

outcomes.name: CSF total-tau (t-tau) protein concentration — mean percentage change from baseline at 24 weeks post-last dose (prespecified key exploratory outcome)

outcomes.quote: Dose-dependent reduction in the CSF total-tau concentration was observed with greater than 50% mean reduction from baseline at 24 weeks post-last dose in the 60 mg (four doses) and 115 mg (two doses) MAPT Rx groups.

limitations: This first-in-human study of MAPT Rx has several limitations mainly due to its small size ( N = 46) as is typical of phase 1 studies.

The MAPT Rx doses evaluated in this study achieved the target t-tau reduction of ~50%, but determining whether this reduction is efficacious will require further evaluation in larger, well-controlled trials.
While there is no statistical rationale for the sample size, it has been selected on the basis of prior experience with generation 2.0 ASOs given by IT bolus injection
Similarly, MAPT Rx -treatment related effects on exploratory biomarkers will require further evaluation in larger trials.

Changes in NfL, Nfh, YKL40 and NRGN levels did not appear to be dose responsive and were not concordant, but interpretation of the clinical meaningfulness of these results is limited due to the combination of assay variability and small sample size.

Lastly, this study was conducted in relatively young participants with mild AD, and it will be important that future studies of MAPT Rx evaluate safety and efficacy in an older population, which may be more representative of late-onset AD.
All study participants were white, and it will be important in larger, later-phase clinical studies of MAPT Rx to include a diverse patient population to adequately evaluate both efficacy and safety.
Limitations of evaluating CSF t-tau and p-tau to index target engagement include the clearance of existing tau protein and reliance on tau transport to the CSF.
While measuring CSF tau protein can index PD activity, it cannot inform on regional differences in MAPT mRNA reduction in CNS tissues.
Steady-state maximal reduction of the concentration of CSF t-tau was not reached during the 13 week treatment period
It is unclear why there is no apparent difference in MAPT Rx CSF trough concentration between the 30 mg and 60 mg MAPT Rx groups.

Comparing the rate of VE observed in our study with that observed in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative is challenging since our patient population was younger (mean age 66 years versus 75 years in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative)

risk_of_bias.quote: The trial was sponsored by Ionis Pharmaceuticals, which provided the study drug (MAPT Rx and placebo). Personnel from Ionis Pharmaceuticals designed the trial in conjunction with collaborators from Biogen, academic investigators and other disease experts.

risk_of_bias.domain: unblinded safety review by sponsor personnel
risk_of_bias.judgement: Dose escalations were authorized by a Formal Safety Monitoring Group composed of sponsor personnel after unblinded review of safety data, although the group is described as independent from study conduct and investigators/participants/sponsor remained blinded to group assignment.
risk_of_bias.quote: A Formal Safety Monitoring Group, composed of sponsor personnel with medical and clinical trial expertise and independent from the conduct of the study, authorized each dose escalation after unblinded review of safety data.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Three of 46 participants (6.5%) voluntarily withdrew during the post-treatment period; exploratory t-tau analyses at 24 weeks post-last dose were reported on reduced numbers (N = 7 for 60 mg, N = 10 for 115 mg) and on N = 5 and N = 3 for the 30 mg and 10 mg groups.
risk_of_bias.quote: Three participants (6.5%) voluntarily withdrew from the study during the post-treatment period: one each from the placebo, 60 mg MAPT Rx cohort (four total doses administered monthly) and 115 mg MAPT Rx cohort

risk_of_bias.judgement: A mid-study protocol amendment changed eligibility, leaving the 60 mg and 115 mg groups with numerically lower baseline CDR Sum of Boxes scores than the other groups.
risk_of_bias.quote: The mean Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) Sum of Boxes score at baseline was numerically lower for MAPT Rx 60 mg and 115 mg treatment groups due to an amendment during the study

risk_of_bias.domain: no inferential statistics / sample size not justified statistically
risk_of_bias.judgement: The document states there was no statistical rationale for the sample size and reports only descriptive summaries; no p-values or confidence intervals are reported.
risk_of_bias.quote: While there is no statistical rationale for the sample size, it has been selected on the basis of prior experience with generation 2.0 ASOs given by IT bolus injection

risk_of_bias.judgement: All participants were white and relatively young, with a much higher proportion of early-onset AD than the general AD population.
risk_of_bias.quote: All study participants were white, and it will be important in larger, later-phase clinical studies of MAPT Rx to include a diverse patient population to adequately evaluate both efficacy and safety.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Cohorts A and B did not transition seamlessly to the LTE and had a variable gap of 5 to 19 months, making their post-treatment biomarker timepoints non-comparable with cohorts C and D.
risk_of_bias.quote: Participants assigned to cohort A or B did not seamlessly transition to LTE part 2 and experienced a variable gap ranging from 5 to 19 months between completion of MAD part 1 at day 253 and registration

disagreements.question: Whether the quantitatively greater increase in ventricular volume in MAPT Rx groups versus placebo represents clinically meaningful ventricular enlargement
disagreements.position: This document holds that although quantitative ventricular volume increases were greater with MAPT Rx, ventricular enlargement was not evident on qualitative neuroradiological review of safety MRI scans and there were no clinical correlates; it notes the etiology of such increases in AD trials remains unclear and that some AD studies report treatment-related increases while others do not.
disagreements.attributed_to: the trial investigators and sponsor authors of this Nature Medicine report (Ionis Pharmaceuticals/Biogen trial team)
disagreements.quote: Importantly, VE was not evident on qualitative neuroradiological review of safety MRI scans, and there were no clinical correlates.

disagreements.question: Whether tau-targeting antibody and vaccine approaches can achieve the same effect as ASO-mediated suppression of tau production
disagreements.position: This document argues that antibody and vaccine approaches target extracellular tau spread and are not predicted to have a major impact on intracellular p-tau, whereas MAPT Rx prevents tau production and should lower all tau species.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this Nature Medicine report
disagreements.quote: Many of the tau-targeting antibody and vaccine approaches currently in development aim to reduce spread of specific extracellular tau species and are not predicted to have a major impact on intracellular p-tau .
